text.p: Hansabank-Latvija, a part of Estonia's largest bank, Hansapank , said on Thursday that it would pursue its aim of becoming a universal bank and shed its image of being a small and expensive bank.

"We are pursuing our policy of becoming a universal bank by orienting both towards individuals...also lowering the threshold for businesses we work with," Aldis Greitans, head of the client service department, told a news conference.
The news conference was called to mark the issue of its thousandth bank card.
"We plan to open two more branches in Riga late this year and are looking for appropriate locations further away from the city centre," Greitans said.
He said the bank also planned to open branches in the biggest regional centres such as Liepaja, Daugavpils and possibly Ventspils in 1998.
"We want in future to orient ourselves more towards medium and small companies."
"There will be more cuts in the commissions we charge," Greitans said.
The bank said it was intensively working on new products for individuals, including bank cards, flexible savings accounts with standing order possibilities.
